symptom: RFC-029 D5c (post-Docling chart-page-detection heuristic) was marked complete in tasks-rfc029 but never implemented in code. No function for chart-page density detection or PictureItem synthesis exists anywhere in the codebase. Without D5c, Docling's Heron RT-DETRv2 layout model does not classify vector charts/bar-charts as PictureItem, so zero <!-- image --> markers are emitted and _recover_picture_results returns [] at converters.py:2225 (guard: _IMAGE_MARKER not in md). The entire picture enrichment pipeline never runs for chart-dominant PDF pages.

symptom: RFC-029 D1 low_content_density gate in validate_tree (helpers.py:1342-1356) rejects trees with chars_per_node < 500 when total_nodes >= 200. This new gate was introduced in commit 08b6eea and has no recovery path -- low_content_density is not in the OCR escalation reasons list (client.py:1008), so the tree simply ERRORs. The threshold of 500 chars/node is too aggressive for legal documents with fine-grained article structure: Penal Code (606 nodes, 408.2 chars/node) and marsoom-33-AR (231 nodes, 459.4 chars/node) were previously healthy PASS trees with near-identical metrics. For federal_decree_law_no_33 EN the drop from ~221 to 54.3 chars/node suggests additional over-fragmentation from _repair_docling_tables char reduction (table whitespace stripping reduced total chars while node count held or grew).

doc: Haftpflicht-Allgemeine-Bedingungen.pdf.pdf, image pie chart about labor distribution in january 2025 - Copy.jpg
symptom: RFC-029 D6 Phase B judge calibration rules were marked complete (task 1.7) but never actually written to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md. The skill file (lines 34-42) still only contains the old RFC-028 D6 guidance about image markers in hierarchical docs. The two new rules specified by RFC-029 D6 are missing: (1) stability rule -- when stored gate verdict is PASS and metrics are byte-identical to the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless citing a specific new defect; (2) severity-anchoring rule -- for flat/chart docs with <1000 chars and zero enrichments, anchor severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when extraction has not regressed. Without these rules, the Opus judge applies inconsistent scrutiny across runs to byte-identical content: Haftpflicht (stored PASS, 132 nodes/53K chars, depth 2 unchanged) gets downgraded to MARGINAL on 'depth-2-too-shallow' scrutiny the Run 12 judge did not apply; image pie chart (stored MARGINAL, 6 nodes/489 chars byte-identical) gets escalated to FAIL on RTL garbling the Run 12 judge did not flag. Both regressions are pure judge non-determinism with no underlying pipeline change.

Without these rules, the Opus judge applies inconsistent scrutiny across runs to byte-identical content: Haftpflicht (stored PASS, 132 nodes/53K chars, depth 2 unchanged) gets downgraded to MARGINAL on 'depth-2-too-shallow' scrutiny the Run 12 judge did not apply; image pie chart (stored MARGINAL, 6 nodes/489 chars byte-identical) gets escalated to FAIL on RTL garbling the Run 12 judge did not flag. suggested_fix: Add the two RFC-029 D6 calibration rules to .claude/skills/corpus-ingest-score/SKILL.md after the existing RFC-028 D6 paragraph: (1) Stability rule: 'When stored gate verdict is PASS and extraction metrics (node count, char count, depth) are within 10% of the prior run, the judge MUST NOT downgrade unless it can cite a specific content-quality defect (garbling, content loss, structural corruption) not present in the prior run finding. Known persistent limitations (e.g. shallow depth for a complex document) that were tolerated in the prior run are NOT grounds for downgrade.' (2) Severity-anchoring rule: 'For flat/chart-heavy docs (content_class starts with flat_) with <1000 total chars and zero picture enrichments, anchor severity to MARGINAL (not FAIL) when the extraction layer has not regressed -- the missing enrichment is a known pipeline gap, not a per-run regression.' Also add a consistency check note to .claude/skills/corpus-score-diff/SKILL.md for byte-identical artifacts across runs.

root_cause: RFC-029 D7 table segmentation (_segment_table_nodes) causes node explosion from 502→~2042 nodes; new low_content_density gate (threshold 500 chars/node) rejects the resulting tree. Both features introduced in commit 08b6eea (RFC-029 implementation).
mechanism: 1. Tree builder (md_to_tree) produces 502-node tree with ~110k chars (same as Run 12). 2. _segment_table_nodes examines nodes for pipe-tables with >=5 rows and >2000 chars. 3. Each qualifying node is split into child nodes (one per table block + inter-table prose). 4. For a hierarchical legal document with multiple embedded tables, this explodes the tree to ~2000+ nodes. 5. validate_tree checks total_nodes >= 200 && chars_per_node < 500 — both conditions met. 6. Tree is rejected with low_content_density ERROR.
why_run_12_passed: RFC-029 code was committed AFTER Run 12 (commit 08b6eea). Run 12 did not have _segment_table_nodes or low_content_density gate.
why_not_repair_docling_tables: _repair_docling_tables strips GFM whitespace (~10% reduction), applied before tree building. This affects markdown char count, not node count. The 4x node explosion is the only mechanism for 54.3 chars/node.
fix_strategy: Lower threshold to ~200 chars/node or exclude child nodes from density check. Add low_content_density to recovery paths in client.py.

root_causes.title: Fence stripping (RFC-029 D3 regression)
root_causes.description: ALL content inside fenced code blocks is discarded. Docling wraps substantial Arabic content in ``` markers for the MOU document. The fence-stripping loop at lines 2724-2726 skips every line while in_fence=True, silently dropping the entire block rather than preserving content and stripping delimiters only.
root_causes.mechanism:
1. Docling exports markdown with fenced blocks wrapping Arabic/mixed-language sections (code-extraction hints)
2. RFC-029 D3 added fence stripping to remove rendering noise
3. Implementation toggles in_fence flag and skips ALL enclosed lines (not just delimiters)
4. Result: 13,564 chars → 1,487 chars (preamble only survives)

doc: قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (1) لسنة 2022 في شأن اللائحة التنفيذية للمرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (33) لسنة 2021 بشأن تنظيم علاقات العمل.pdf
pdf_text_layer: none (scanned, verified via PyMuPDF get_text() == '' on all 21 pages)
root_cause_function: index() Fix-3 OCR-escalation 'keep-best' guardrail (RFC-029 D4 / Task 3.3)
root_cause_summary: _repeating_token_density() returns 0.0 whenever a text has <20 alnum tokens (line 1094-1095). The RFC-029 D4 keep-best comparator (added since Run 12) computes _pre_density=_repeating_token_density(pre_retry_text) and only accepts the OCR-retry's richer result when _post_density < _pre_density*0.80. For scanned/no-text-layer PDFs like this one, the pre-retry pass (do_ocr=False by default, RFC-021 QF1 deferral) produces near-empty/garbled text, so pre_retry token count is almost always <20, forcing _pre_density=0.0. The inequality _post_density < 0.0*0.80 is then arithmetically impossible to satisfy, so retry_wins=False unconditionally whenever the pre-retry snapshot is short-and-garbled -- exactly the population of documents this OCR-escalation retry exists to rescue. On revert (line 1144-1147) only result/ok/reason are rolled back to the pre-retry (near-empty) tree; md_content, pic_results and tmp_md_path are NOT reverted, so the tree-path and flat-path diverge on which content survives depending on whether the pre-retry reason was node_count<3 (flat routing still uses the good md_content) or garbling (raises outright). For this document the net effect is partial content survival (14.8k of an original ~48k), consistent with only part of the OCR-recovered structure surviving the reverted tree gate while flat-routing salvages a fraction via a separate, less request-specific path.
suggested_fix: Guard _repeating_token_density (or its D4 caller) so a pre-retry text with <20 tokens is treated as 'no reliable density signal' rather than density=0.0 -- e.g. return None and short-circuit retry_wins=True (any real recovery beats near-empty content) instead of running it through the '<' comparison that is unsatisfiable against a floor of 0. Also make the revert at line 1144-1147 restore md_content/tmp_md_path/pic_results in lockstep with result/ok/reason so tree-path and flat-path never diverge on which markdown was actually used.
confidence: high (verified against source at client.py:1083-1148, helpers.py:863-891 for _is_garbled_blob empty-blob=True, and confirmed via PyMuPDF that all 21 pages carry zero embedded text)

doc: قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (106) لسنة 2022 بشأن اللائحة التنفيذية للمرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (9) لسنة 2022 بشأن أعمال الخدمة المساعدة.pdf
symptom: Run 12 MARGINAL (179 nodes / 26,027 chars, depth-0 flat hierarchy) regressed to Run 13 FAIL (11 nodes / 2,022 chars, ~92% content loss); extraction now starts at Article 4 and ends abruptly instead of covering the full 15-page executive regulation.
root_cause: RFC-029 D4 (Task 3.3) 'keep-best' OCR-retry comparison in client.py (commit 08b6eea) replaced the previous unconditional `retry_wins = True` (post_retry_chars > pre_retry_chars branch) with a repeating-token-density guard. `_repeating_token_density()` (client.py:1083-1096) returns a hardcoded 0.0 whenever the input has fewer than 20 alnum tokens (line 1094). This doc is a 15-page fully scanned/image-only PDF (confirmed: PyPDF2 extracts 0 chars on every page) that is well under MAX_DOCLING_PAGES=150, so it never enters the chunked-Docling route — the truncation is not a chunking artifact. Instead it takes the LOW_CONTENT_OCR_CHAR_FLOOR retry path (client.py:1001-1014): the first, non-forced Docling pass yields near-empty/garbled markdown (a short mid-document fragment happening to start around 'Article 4'), reason='node_count<3', total_chars<300, triggering the force_full_page_ocr escalation. The escalation legitimately recovers far more content (post_retry_chars > pre_retry_chars), landing in the `else` branch at client.py:1111-1143. There, `_pre_garble_flag = _is_garbled_blob(pre_retry_text)` is true for the short garbled fragment, so the code computes `_pre_density = _repeating_token_density(pre_retry_text)`. Because the pre-retry fragment has <20 alnum tokens, `_pre_density` is forced to 0.0 regardless of its actual content. The subsequent check `_density_improved = _post_density < _pre_density * 0.80` then evaluates as `_post_density < 0.0`, which is unsatisfiable for any non-negative density value — `retry_wins` is unconditionally False whenever the pre-retry fragment is short-but-garbled. `result = pre_retry_result` (client.py:1145) then discards the complete, OCR-recovered markdown and keeps the short pre-retry garbled fragment (whatever partial/garbled text the first Docling pass happened to pull off a mid-document page range) as the persisted content — exactly matching the observed 'starts at Article 4, ends abruptly' truncation and the 179->11 node / 26,027->2,022 char collapse. This is a distinct code-level mechanism from the cluster's converters.py _repair_docling_tables/NFKC total-collapse finding: it lives in client.py's RFC-029 D4 retry-arbitration logic, not in the markdown-generation/table-repair code path, and produces partial-fragment truncation rather than 0-block total collapse.
code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:1083-1147 (function-local `_repeating_token_density` at 1083-1096, retry-arbitration branch at 1098-1147, specifically the short-text degenerate case at line 1094 `if len(tokens) < 20: return 0.0` feeding the unsatisfiable comparison at line 1131 `_density_improved = _post_density < _pre_density * 0.80`)
suggested_fix: In `_repeating_token_density`, do not silently collapse short inputs to 0.0 density (which biases the RFC-029 D4 comparison to always reject the retry). Either (a) return `None`/a sentinel for <20-token inputs and treat that case as 'density undecidable -> retry_wins = True' (mirroring the pre-existing behavior before RFC-029 D4), since a growth in char count from a too-short-to-score fragment to a scoreable OCR result is itself strong evidence of recovery; or (b) fall back to `_is_garbled_blob` post-retry check alone (as already done in the equal-char-count tie-break branch at line 1100-1110) when the pre-retry token count is below the 20-token floor. Add a regression test with a <20-token garbled pre-retry fragment and a much longer, non-garbled post-retry OCR result to assert retry_wins=True.
